title: Neural circuits for valence updating in social memory.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data files exist to open. I checked Europe PMC (paper is closed access, not in PubMed Central, hasSuppl=N, so no supplementary file listing), the Europe PMC data-links endpoint for PubMed ID 42424460 (the only link is Mouse Genome Informatics citing the paper for mouse strains, not a dataset), and searched Zenodo, Dryad, figshare, OSF, DANDI (the standard repository for neurophysiology recordings) and Mendeley Data by DOI/title/keyword: all returned zero records. The publisher page and its supplementary-material URL both return HTTP 403.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the experiments comes from the abstract plus a search-result summary of the paper: a mouse ventral CA1 (vCA1, part of the hippocampus) to basolateral amygdala (BLA) to nucleus accumbens (NAc) circuit, memory-tagging of 'engram' neurons, in vivo calcium imaging of BLA and NAc neuron responses, optogenetic manipulation, and patch-clamp synaptic recordings. No sample sizes, neuron counts or file formats were visible anywhere.

a1_downloadable.note: No downloadable data found anywhere. Closed-access Science paper with no PubMed Central copy, no Europe PMC supplementary files, and zero hits in Zenodo, Dryad, figshare, OSF, DANDI and Mendeley Data; publisher page returns 403 so even the supplementary PDF is unreachable. Best case the source values sit inside subscription-gated supplementary files, which is still not a downloadable dataset.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessable: no files. Any label (for example 'does this neuron respond to the aggressor') would have to be constructed from raw calcium traces aligned to behaviour, not read from a column.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not assessable: no calcium traces, spike times, behaviour tracking or electrophysiology files are available.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessable: no files to inspect for units (dF/F, Hz, pA, mV).

a5_enough_rows.note: Unknown and unverifiable. Typical circuit papers of this design use roughly 5-15 mice per group; neuron counts are not stated in the abstract.

a6_fits_laptop.note: If processed calcium traces were released they would almost certainly be well under 1 GB and laptop-friendly; this is the only killer that is not a problem.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot compare counts: there is no download and the paper text itself is behind a paywall.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable. Labels would be experimenter-assigned conditions (neutral vs aggressor conspecific, pre- vs post-defeat), which is good provenance in principle, but engram 'tagging' labels depend on an activity-dependent reporter threshold that is itself a processing choice.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: without the recordings there is nothing to train on or test against.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use brain-cell activity patterns to predict whether a mouse now treats a familiar mouse as friend or threat
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on calcium-imaging traces (a fluorescence readout of neural activity) from basolateral amygdala and nucleus accumbens neurons while a test mouse meets familiar, novel and newly-aggressive mice. Number of neurons and sessions: unknown, nothing was released.
plain_idea.predict: Output would be the social valence the mouse assigns to the encountered individual (approach vs avoid, before vs after being defeated by it), with the true answer coming from video-scored behaviour and the experimenter-controlled defeat protocol.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Systems neuroscientists studying social behaviour would learn whether valence updating is readable from population activity alone and how far ahead of behaviour it appears; it is moot here because the recordings were never deposited.

ml_idea: Decode social valence (approach vs avoid a specific familiar conspecific, before vs after social defeat by it) from ventral CA1 / basolateral amygdala / nucleus accumbens population calcium activity, with mice held out to test cross-animal generalisation. Not executable: no recordings were deposited.

effort.compute_note: No estimate possible because no data was located; nothing was downloaded or timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Search the repositories for a deposit keyed to the DOI or title. Done: Zenodo, Dryad, figshare, OSF, DANDI and Mendeley Data all return zero, and Europe PMC lists no supplementary files. That check alone kills it in minutes.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails outright: closed-access Science paper, no PubMed Central copy, no supplementary files via Europe PMC, publisher blocked (403), and no deposit in any neurophysiology or general repository, so there is no dataset to model. Even if the supplement were reachable it would hold summary statistics for a small-n mouse circuit study, not a feature/label table.
